hints: Focus on what aqueous potassium hydroxide actually removes from the gas mixture after combustion.
Write the two complete combustion equations and use the volume ratio to find the $\text{CO}_2$ made from $10 \text{ cm}^3$ of methane and from $10 \text{ cm}^3$ of ethane separately.
Remember water is liquid after cooling, so only $\text{CO}_2$ is absorbed, add the two $\text{CO}_2$ volumes together to get the total absorbed.
walkthrough:
**Spot what the alkali absorbs**

Think like a detective. After sparking and cooling, what gases are left?

Complete combustion makes $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. After cooling, water is liquid, so the residual gas is $\text{CO}_2$ plus excess $\text{O}_2$. Aqueous $\text{KOH}$ absorbs acidic $\text{CO}_2$ but not $\text{O}_2$. So volume absorbed = total volume of $\text{CO}_2$ formed.

**Find $\text{CO}_2$ from methane**

Write the balanced equation for methane:
$$\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
At same T and P, gas volume ratio = mole ratio. 1 volume of $\text{CH}_4$ gives 1 volume of $\text{CO}_2$. So $10 \text{ cm}^3$ of methane gives $10 \text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$.

**Find $\text{CO}_2$ from ethane**

Now write the balanced equation for ethane:
$$2\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 + 7\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 4\text{CO}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Here 2 volumes of ethane give 4 volumes of $\text{CO}_2$, a 1 to 2 ratio. So $10 \text{ cm}^3$ of ethane gives $20 \text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$.

**Add to get total absorbed**

Just add the two contributions together:
$$V(\text{CO}_2) = 10 \text{ cm}^3 + 20 \text{ cm}^3 = 30 \text{ cm}^3$$
That is the volume removed by the alkali.

options.A: Incorrect. $15 \text{ cm}^3$ would come from averaging or halving the true total. You must treat methane and ethane separately and remember ethane gives two $\text{CO}_2$ per molecule, not one.
options.B: Incorrect. $20 \text{ cm}^3$ is only the $\text{CO}_2$ from the $10 \text{ cm}^3$ of ethane. This trap forgets to add the $10 \text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$ made from the methane.
options.C: Correct. Methane gives $10 \text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$ and ethane gives $20 \text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$. After cooling water is liquid, so $\text{KOH}$ absorbs all $30 \text{ cm}^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$.
options.D: Incorrect. $40 \text{ cm}^3$ overcounts the $\text{CO}_2$. It may come from thinking both hydrocarbons give 2 $\text{CO}_2$ each, but methane ($\text{CH}_4$) has only one carbon and so gives only one $\text{CO}_2$.
